what: Church & Dwight makes household and personal care products. Arm & Hammer baking soda and laundry detergent, Trojan condoms, OxiClean, Waterpik, Vitafusion vitamins and Hero acne patches are among its brands.
customers: American households through supermarkets, mass retailers, club stores and online.
money: US household and personal care brands
the same brands outside the United States
moat: A portfolio deliberately split between value brands that sell well in downturns and premium brands that sell well in good times, with leading share in several small categories.
risks: Growth slowed to about 2% last year as volumes softened
Private label competes directly with its value brands
Some acquired brands such as Flawless have been written down
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
opportunities: Return on invested capital of 13% with modest debt of $2.4 billion
Its value brands gain share when consumers trade down
A long record of acquiring small brands and growing them through its distribution
watch: Organic volume growth and gross margin.
